mentions.name: GNSS/RTK-based robot lawnmower
mentions.description: An autonomous robot lawnmower built by buying a cheap, non-functioning second-hand mower, tearing out its circuit board, and coding a new ROS2-based stack so it roams the lawn on GPS with RTK (base station in the charging station). The friend handles electronics while the author focuses on software; the next milestone is testing a simple bounding box where the mower drives until it reaches an edge and then randomly picks a new direction.
mentions.problem: Existing robot lawnmowers were quite expensive, especially when the builder started out.
mentions.source_excerpt:
Building a GNSS/RTK-based lawnmower.

The existing ones were quite expensive, especially when I started out. A friend had the idea to get a cheap/non-functioning lawnmower second hand, and tear out the circuit board. We're in the process of coding up a new ROS2 based stack that will roam the lawn on GPS with RTK in the charging station.
